results.title: A plain command runs and its output comes back
Pipes and quotes behave like a normal shell
The working folder persists between commands
An interactive program can be typed into (Python prompt)
Ctrl+C interrupts a running command
Resizing the window reaches the program
Non-English text and emoji survive the round trip
Five thousand lines of output arrive complete and in order
When a program exits, its exit code is reported
A short typo gives 'command not found' and does not start planning
A sentence typed at the prompt becomes a task, and 'n' cancels it
Known limit: a sentence starting with a real command runs that command
results.detail: Documented behaviour. 'Send to agents' (next scenario) is the way around it.

results.title: 'Send to agents' passes apostrophes, ? and * through untouched
Declining the plan runs nothing and records it as cancelled
With no agent installed it says so and exits cleanly
With one agent enabled it skips planning and runs the task directly
If the planner replies with nonsense, the whole task goes to one agent
A failed step is retried on another agent, with the reason and token count
If every agent fails, it stops and says which steps were skipped
Outside a git repository, a Codex step is rerouted with an explanation
Antigravity reporting success after a blocked action is treated as a failure
Token counts are totalled and logged for the dashboard
By default every saver rule, the handoff note and the low-effort flag reach the agents
Switching the savers off in Settings removes them
A note an agent asks to keep is saved in the project's .relaycrew folder
The next task is told the saved notes and what was done before
With project memory switched off, nothing is saved or sent
Typing in the command box and pressing Enter runs the command
The 'Approve and run' button starts the plan
The 'Cancel' button declines the plan and nothing runs
'Send to agents' sends the text as a task, punctuation intact
A switch changed in Settings is saved
If the task is interrupted while waiting, the Approve button goes away
REAL: the planner returns a usable plan for a mixed everyday task
REAL: Codex writes code and tests, Antigravity documents it, and the tests pass
